answer: Yes, Verizon is a capital-intensive business based on FY 2022 data. In its FY 2022 10-K, Verizon explicitly states under Risk Factors that "We require a significant amount of capital to operate and grow our business." In FY 2022, Verizon had capital expenditures (including capitalized software) of $23,087 million, which represents approximately 16.87% of its total operating revenues ($136,835 million). Additionally, as of December 31, 2022, the company reported net property, plant and equipment of $107,434 million.
rationale: The company explicitly notes in Item 1A that it requires a significant amount of capital to operate and grow. Quantitative metrics confirm this: capital expenditures were $23,087 million (approx. 16.9% of revenues of $136,835 million) and net property, plant and equipment was $107,434 million at year-end 2022.
